journeys.title: Preparing for a routine check-up
journeys.who: Otis, 65, has two lab reports from different labs a year apart.
journeys.goal: See what changed between the two reports, and write down questions before the check-up.
starterQuestions: Which of these results would you like to recheck, and when?

journeys.title: Organising records before seeing a new doctor
journeys.who: Donovan, 64, is moving to a new practice and has a summary, a letter and a lab report.
journeys.goal: Build one tidy list of medicines (current, stopped, unclear) and recent results to bring along.
starterQuestions: Should I keep taking all of the medicines on the current list?

journeys.title: Helping a parent prepare for an appointment
journeys.who: An adult child is helping Santo, 68, make sense of a results printout, a portal message and a visit summary.
journeys.goal: Understand what each paper says, spot repeated tests, and bring a one-page brief to the appointment.
starterQuestions: Is there anything we should bring or do before the next appointment?

Eastgate Health Centre

Visit date: March 22, 2025   Reason: General examination of patient

Vital signs: BP 109/73 mmHg, Pulse 90 /min, Weight 87.7 kg, BMI 30.1 kg/m2

Results from this visit:
  Blood glucose: 70.8 mg/dL (ref 70 to 100)
  Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL
  Potassium: 4.9 mmol/L
  Carbon dioxide (CO2): 27.6 mmol/L

Your current medications:
  - lisinopril 10 MG, every day
  - simvastatin 20 MG, as needed
  - prasugrel 10 MG
  - losartan potassium 50 MG Oral Tablet, as needed
  - metoprolol succinate 25 MG ER

No longer taking:
  - nitroglycerin 0.4 MG Sublingual Tablet (stopped June 28, 2024)

Previous prescriptions on file:
  - December 13, 2022: Ibuprofen 200 MG

Plan:
  - Diabetic diet
  - Exercise therapy
  - Prescribed activity/exercise education
  - Next appointment: April 5, 2025 (Encounter for check up)

documents.text:
Old Mill Community Clinic
Date: March 27, 2025

Re: Donovan Johns, DOB January 1, 1961

Dear colleague,

I saw Donovan on March 22, 2025 for general examination of patient.
He continues on simvastatin 20 mg PRN (as needed).
He is currently taking metoprolol succinate 25 mg ER as needed.
He is currently taking lisinopril 10 mg once a day.
He is currently taking prasugrel 10 mg.
He is no longer taking nitroglycerin 0.4 mg.
He is no longer taking ticagrelor 90 mg.
There is an older prescription for ibuprofen 200 mg from 2022 in the record.
Results today: blood glucose 70.8 mg/dL, urea nitrogen (BUN) 8.1 mg/dL, calcium 9.7 mg/dL.
We discussed the care plan: diabetic diet.
We discussed the care plan: exercise therapy.
We will see him again on April 5, 2025.

Kind regards,
Dr. L. Fournier
